_help: Six shifts. Each: learn cards, drill questions (answer = index into choices), hands-on checklist.

shifts.name: First Rounds
shifts.skills: Vital signs: pulse, blood pressure, breathing rate, temperature, oxygen saturation
shifts.intro: Vitals tell us how a patient is doing before they can. Hints are on, so read each one carefully.
shifts.checkpoint: Take a full set of vitals on a partner. They score you with this checklist.

learn.title: Pulse
learn.text: Use two fingers on the radial artery. Count for a full 60 seconds if the rhythm is irregular, and note the strength.

learn.title: Blood pressure
learn.text: Right cuff size, arm at heart level, patient seated and calm. A reading far below their usual means act.

learn.title: Breathing rate
learn.text: Count it while it looks like you are still taking the pulse, so the patient does not change how they breathe.

learn.title: Temperature
learn.text: Choose the route that suits the patient and clean the thermometer between patients.

learn.title: Oxygen saturation
learn.text: Warm, clean finger without nail polish. Below 90% is urgent.

checklist: Wash hands and explain the check to your partner.
Take pulse for 60 seconds and record rate and rhythm.
Measure blood pressure with the correct cuff size.
Count breathing rate without telling your partner.
Record temperature and oxygen saturation.
Record all values accurately and say who you would call.

shifts.name: Comfort Round
shifts.intro: Comfort is care. Watch the comfort meter: rushing or exposing a patient makes it drop.
shifts.checkpoint: Make an occupied bed with a partner and talk through a bed bath and oral care on a mannequin or partner.

learn.title: Occupied bed
learn.text: Explain, close the curtain, roll the patient to one side, work one half of the bed, then roll him to the other side. Keep him covered.

learn.title: Bed bath
learn.text: Uncover and wash one part at a time. Face first, then arms, chest, legs and back. Use comfortably warm water and ask how he feels.

learn.title: Oral care
learn.text: Sit the patient up if it is safe. If he cannot help, gently clean teeth and gums and watch for choking.

learn.title: Comfort meter
learn.text: Exposing a patient, cold water or hurrying all lower comfort and dignity.

drill.label: Bed making
drill.prompt: What do you do first for an occupied bed?

drill.label: Bed bath
drill.prompt: How much do you uncover at once?

drill.label: Bed bath
drill.prompt: Which area do you usually wash first?

drill.label: Oral care
drill.prompt: He cannot help with his mouth. Best action?
choices: Gently clean teeth and gums with a soft brush

drill.label: Comfort
drill.prompt: He says the water is too cold. You…

checklist: Wash hands, explain and close the curtain or screen.
Strip and remake one half of an occupied bed, then roll and finish the other half.
Keep the patient covered and warm during the bed bath.
Wash in the right order, one area at a time.
Do oral care on a mannequin or partner, talking through each step.
Leave the patient comfortable and the bed tidy.

shifts.name: Sharps Room
shifts.intro: Sharps need full focus. Learn the sequence, then drill it until it is automatic.
shifts.checkpoint: Practise cannulation and injections on a training arm or model while a peer scores you on the checklist.

learn.title: Prepare
learn.text: Wash hands, explain, and gather cannula, tourniquet, swabs, dressing, flush and a sharps bin before you start.

learn.title: Vein site
learn.text: Forearm veins are often good. Avoid bent joints, bruised areas and arms that should not be used.

learn.title: Cannulation
learn.text: Tourniquet on, clean the skin and let it dry, insert at a shallow angle, release the tourniquet, secure and flush gently. Stop if there is pain or swelling.

learn.title: Injections
learn.text: IM is about 90 degrees into a large muscle such as the deltoid or ventrogluteal. SC is 45 to 90 degrees into fatty tissue. Never recap needles.

drill.label: Flushing
drill.prompt: Pain and swelling as you flush. You…
choices: Stop and tell the nurse in charge

drill.label: Sharps
choices: In the sharps bin, not recapped

drill.label: Injections
drill.prompt: An IM injection goes in at about…

checklist: Wash hands, explain and gather equipment on a training arm.
Choose a suitable vein site and apply the tourniquet.
Clean the skin, let it dry and insert at the correct angle.
Secure the cannula and flush gently while watching the site.
Name the correct sites and angles for IM and SC injections.
Dispose of sharps without recapping and wash hands.

shifts.name: Medication Round
shifts.skills: Oral, IM, IV, SC medicines and dose calculations
shifts.intro: Safe medicines mean checking every time. The five rights never get skipped.
shifts.checkpoint: Prepare and check a mock medication round with labelled empty containers, and solve dose calculations on paper.

learn.title: Five rights
learn.text: Check all five against the prescription and the wristband every time.

learn.title: Allergies
learn.text: Ask about allergies and read the chart. If a drug matches an allergy, hold it and tell the nurse in charge.

learn.title: Dose maths
learn.text: Example: 500 mg wanted with 250 mg tablets: 500 ÷ 250 = 2 tablets. Always show your working.

learn.title: Drip rate
learn.text: Example: 1000 ml over 8 hours = 125 ml per hour.

drill.label: Five rights
drill.prompt: Which is NOT one of the five rights?

drill.label: Check
drill.prompt: How do you confirm the patient?

drill.label: Dose
drill.prompt: Wanted 500 mg. Tablets are 250 mg. How many?

drill.label: Allergy
drill.prompt: Penicillin allergy, drug is amoxicillin. You…
choices: Hold it and tell the nurse in charge

drill.label: Records
choices: Record at the end of the day

checklist: Check the five rights on a mock prescription with labelled containers.
Check the wristband against the chart.
Solve two dose calculations on paper with working.
Calculate one drip rate on paper.
Describe what you do when an allergy is found.
Record the mock dose correctly.

shifts.name: Front Door
shifts.intro: Patients arrive faster than we can see them. Sort them by urgency before the waiting room overflows.
shifts.checkpoint: Triage role-play with classmates using printed case cards. Explain your reasoning aloud.

learn.title: Triage
learn.text: The sickest patient is seen first. Under-triaging a critical patient is the most dangerous mistake.

learn.title: Immediate
learn.text: Airway, breathing or circulation problems, such as chest pain with very low blood pressure and a fast pulse.

learn.title: Urgent
learn.text: Breathless but talking, significant pain, abnormal vitals that are not yet critical.

learn.title: Routine
learn.text: Normal vitals and minor problems. They can wait, but tell them what to expect and recheck.

drill.label: Waiting
drill.prompt: A routine patient asks how long. You…

checklist: Explain your triage reasoning aloud on a printed case card.
Sort three case cards from most to least urgent.
Name one sign that makes a patient Immediate.
Tell a waiting patient what to expect.
Recheck a waiting patient and record it.
Hand over the order of urgency to a partner.

shifts.name: Golden Hour
shifts.skills: Everything together, ending with an SBAR handover
shifts.intro: The full night shift. Skills from every shift come back. Prioritise well, then hand over.
shifts.checkpoint: Do a supervised practical assessment covering vitals, care, cannulation, medication and handover, signed off by a lecturer or clinician.

learn.title: Prioritise
learn.text: See the most unstable patient first, then scheduled tasks.

learn.title: Medicines due
learn.text: Check wristband, allergies and dose before any medicine.

learn.title: New admission
learn.text: Check identity, take baseline vitals and make the patient comfortable.

learn.title: SBAR
learn.text: Say who the patient is and the problem, the background, your assessment, and what you recommend.

drill.label: Admission
drill.prompt: A new admission arrives. First you…
choices: Check identity and take baseline vitals

checklist: Take a full set of vitals and record them.
Give personal care with privacy and dignity.
Do cannulation on a model with the checklist.
Prepare and check a mock medication round.
Triage three case cards aloud.
Give an SBAR handover, signed off by a lecturer or clinician.
